---
title: "Itoshi Sae, the best character in Blue Lock"

edition: translation
language: en
audience: everyone
publication_id: 6465422

A Japanese footballer and a member of Real Madrid's second team or youth team in the world of *Blue Lock*, Itoshi Sae is often portrayed as an arrogant character and a stepping stone for the protagonists, especially Itoshi Rin, his younger brother.

![Itoshi Sae](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/304ecdd4-a244-4669-b4fd-e2179c2cda65_736x1103.jpeg)

What tends to go unnoticed, however, is his story with his brother and the background importance he has in the creation of the Blue Lock Project by Jinpachi Ego.

From a very young age—at seven or eight years old—Sae played football for a local team and was already considered a prodigy. His brother soon came to admire him and recognize his own potential. Together, they dreamed of becoming the best strikers in the world, like almost every character in the series.

As he grew a little older, still a teenager, he went to play for Spain's biggest team, on football's biggest stage: Europe. He came back changed. He no longer wanted to be the best striker; he considered it impossible. Instead, he had a new dream: to become the greatest midfielder of all. After returning to Japan, he explained his new outlook to his brother in a very rude way.

And in this tense conversation—shown in a flashback during a very important match against Japan's U-20 team, which would decide whether the Blue Lock Project would be canceled—it's easy to miss certain details, such as the fact that Sae still dreamed of his brother becoming the best striker in the world. Rin is quick to turn hostile toward his brother, and Sae doubles down instead of trying to calm things down.

![Itoshi Sae](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/e20076fa-9a3a-4c52-8567-04ef69e57fee_736x736.jpeg)

Beyond his relationship with his brother, Sae plays an important part in the creation of Blue Lock. Jinpachi Ego has strong opinions about football and Japanese football in particular. In the early chapters, he explains that he does not believe Japan suffers from a lack of talent. Rather, he believes a social mechanism destroys emerging talent by sending players abroad too early, without building an ecosystem to nurture them in Japan.

To me, this clearly refers to Itoshi Sae, a talented young player whose potential everyone recognized, but who becomes disillusioned with his own prospects. He becomes disillusioned not only with his own talent, but also with Japan's ability to develop others like him. He clearly places himself above the Japanese players while still considering himself inferior to a select group of geniuses of his generation—probably Kaiser and Loki, the names that come to mind now.

![Itoshi Sae](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/d8131029-cf59-481c-9756-f6d4aaac75c0_736x552.jpeg)

I admit I have a strong dislike of the character because of how he behaves toward the main cast, but I recognize this as a narrative device that casts him as an antagonist beyond his obvious character flaw. He still carries the dream of becoming the best of all players in a particular position, wanting to face and surpass players like Charles Chevalier and Vivian Hugo, both from France.

![Itoshi Sae](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/c071d891-38eb-4bee-8d73-d656a085b01b_736x736.jpeg)

All of his appearances take place in a Japanese context, with a non-combative culture that he despises. So the question remains: given his ideals, how does he interact with those he considers his equals?

We have only seen him in action for Japan's U-20 team in the friendly against Blue Lock. He will play again for the new Japan team at the U-20 World Cup, now alongside the main cast and Yoichi Isagi, in whom he has already shown interest, against the other major names mentioned once the group stages are over.

I look forward to his next appearances, and I am certain the character opens the door to philosophical discussions about the path each player on the field should follow.
